Name: Seaside Interiors
Author: risrain
Description:
[b][u]2.0 OVERHAUL:[/u][/b]
- Framing is now all one matching color, with a choice of color. The base texture was cleaned up a little (removed speckles/lines on the framing beams) and the wood texture used elsewhere was applied. The town, farmhouse interior, and greenhouse interior are 3 separate choices for framing color. (Windows are included in this) Tiny note: The screen that shows while Clint breaks open geodes will always have black framing. 
- Furniture color is now more standardized with a variety of color options - although you can choose to keep the original 3 colors and the mismatching that comes with it (a problem with the vanilla maps, not this mod). You can choose between everything matching (the multiple copies of end tables, dressers, tables, etc have been edited to be different styles) or the same color applied to the range of woods (so you'll have a light, medium, and dark). 
- The town interior kitchen counters & cabinets' wood is now recolored along with the furniture when you choose a new color in the config. 
- Doors have the same color choices as the framing with a separate config option.
- There is now a transom window above the door that is the same color [s]as the framing[/s]. 
- Standardized the color options of framing, furniture and doors. I couldn't pick a reasonable number and so there are 20 (twenty!) different colors. I think the furniture looks silly with the less natural colors (such as red) but I figured I'd still include them as options. (For what it's worth, this number is AFTER I culled a bunch of colors...)
- Changed the texture of the 1.6 kitchen counters to be more speckly/more like laminate. Standardized the darker wood tone of the default to match the "walnut" of the furniture. Replaced whatever those weird grey dvd looking things were in the upper cabinets with actual kitchen items (glass jars, pot, canisters). 
- Certain locations have unique edits for framing color, furniture, etc - this is toggleable. You can also toggle the few minor map edits. Hopefully this (along with single framing & furniture color) improves compatibility with other mods that edit the map. Most of the map edits fix beds, because the vanilla double bed and single bed's footboards are indistinguishable and there are cases where the double bed used parts of the single bed (and vice versa). 
- Edits to the special event tilesheets (heart events and such) are now a toggeable config - the few that needed to match the furniture are separate and will always apply. (i.e. A heart event for Leah and the special omelet cutscene for Gus)  
- Added crib bedding & wood color options
- Replaced pretty much all paintings from the towninterior & towninterior_2 sheets with public domain artwork (vastly scaled down) 
- Added compatibility for Altar of Yoba Replacement - a very basic rug replacement while in Pierre's. I do not have that mod installed so could not test it in game.
- Lots of tiny fixes


Retook the vast majority of the screenshots (ensuring this time it was set to 100% scale...). The only visual mods used were:
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5255]DaisyNiko's Earth Recolour[/url]﻿
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/4697]Vintage Interface 2.0[/url] + [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/20754]1.6 Fix[/url]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/6733]Seaside Valley[/url] (obviously)

While not required, there are so many options to choose from that I highly recommend everyone use: 
[font=Georgia][color=#8e7cc3][size=4][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url][/size][/color][/font]
In addition to being more readable than the config textfile, you can change the options while in game, which is especially helpful for deciding which of the wood colors is your favorite :) 

-----

Interior & interior-related tilesheets recolored to complement my Seaside Valley exteriors mod. This includes all the furniture tilesheets - My goal was not to totally redo a lot of those (that's what the Alternative Textures mod is for :) ) but instead make the vanilla one more palatable. I also wanted to standardize wood colors so it would look more seamless. I also made sure the Joja-related items had a green and blue version, just like my exteriors mod.

This supports all the languages that were represented by the vanilla files.

For slightly more advanced users - Seaside Interiors has some textures that are OVERLAYS only and I took care to stick to the original shape of the items underneath most of the time. This means if there is something you don't like but you don't want to disable the entire tilesheet via the config, you can simply delete that part of the tilesheet while using the rest. (This would require you to use some kind of graphics software) Please see the included text file for details!

I have also added a zip file under "Optional Files" that has my layered file (I use Affinity Photo 2.6.5 - not 3.0+ from Canva, but that one is free) for making matching wood recolors of other mods. There is also a guide, a PSD conversion of the affinity document, and rhodox's wood texture. Full disclosure - I never thought about sharing when I made the file originally so the layers/groups are a bit of a mess. If you make and share any recolors using the wood texture, YOU MUST credit Rhodox for it. (And a link back here would be nice <3 I'd also just like to see what people do with it!) 

[u][b]Known Issues: [/b][/u]
- For SVE Compatibility, please see:  [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/45019]Seaside Valley Expanded (SVE Compat)[/url]
- There will be some graphical flaws with Less Ugly Town Interiors because I have not recolored its tilesheets. For example, Pam & Penny's trailer has a kitchen cabinet that hangs open that looks like the vanilla textures. [s]I will be working on recoloring these but no ETA and they will provided without any code. [/s] Anybody is free to make these recolors with the layered file I provided and share them. 
- Any mod that modifies the maps of interiors may have some issues. I only tested the vanilla and SVE because that is what I personally use. There are too many mods out there for me to possibly test all of them, unfortunately.
- When you have bought all the backpacks at Pierre's, it covers the "for sale" thing with a bar of solid color, and I have NO idea where this comes from. It could be hardcoded for all I know. I included a picture of the issue.
- During Emily's 2-heart dream sequence, her bedspread may be the wrong color if another mod is editing that part of Cursors - in my case, it was Vintage Interface v2. There is an updated manifest that should fix this. If it's an issue with other interface mods, they can be added to the manifest the same as VI2 and it should fix it.
- During Leah's art website cutscene, the overlay texture is applied a few pixels off - when I tested without any mods it still looked like that, so I think it's a vanilla issue that I can't fix. (I did use a mod to force the heart events to play, so maybe somehow that contributed to the glitches) 

As usual please report any issues or conflicts you find! I can't possibly test with all mods.

Note: The license on the GitHub is ONLY for the assets I have made myself. There are plenty of textures that fall under other creators'
terms and that must be respected.
[b]Please feel free to share any important edits (like if a patch breaks something) publicly if I do not respond within a month.[/b]
